desc:
Several frogs sit by a pond. A frog that croaks says the word "croak" by emitting its letters c, r, o, a, k one after another, in this order, with no pause. A frog can only start a new croak after it finished the previous one. Different frogs may croak at the same time, so their letters interleave in one recording.

The string croak is the whole recording. Return the minimum number of different frogs needed to produce it, or -1 if the recording cannot be a mixture of complete croaks (a letter is out of order or some croak is unfinished).

"croakcroak"  -> 1   (one frog croaks twice)
"crcoakroak"  -> 2   (two overlapping croaks)
"croakcrook"  -> -1  (the second word is broken)
"croa"        -> -1  (unfinished croak)
constraints: croak consists only of the letters c, r, o, a and k
hints: Whenever a letter other than c arrives it must continue some frog that is currently waiting for exactly that letter. A c starts a croak.

Keep a counter for how many frogs are in each stage: just said c, said cr, said cro, said croa. A letter moves one frog from the stage before to the next, and the recording is invalid if no frog is in the stage before.
The number of frogs needed is the largest number of frogs that are mid-croak at the same time. Frogs that said k are free again. At the end no frog may be mid-croak.
editorial: Frogs are interchangeable, so only the number of frogs in each stage matters. Let cnt[i] be the number of frogs that have said the first i + 1 letters of croak and now wait for the next letter (i = 0..3). On c a croak begins: cnt[0] and the number of busy frogs go up. On r, o, a one frog moves from stage i - 1 to stage i; if no frog is in the stage before, the letter has no owner and the recording is invalid. On k a frog leaves stage 3 and becomes free, which lowers the number of busy frogs.

A frog that has just finished can start the next croak, so the number of frogs needed is the maximum number of simultaneously busy frogs. If someone is still busy after the last letter, a croak is unfinished and the answer is -1. This is one pass with four counters: O(n) time and O(1) space.
